A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same noise-corrected GRPO work. All main-text and appendix pages are readable, and the methods, equations, figures, and tables can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results on GSM8K and APPS under synthetic reward corruption and learned reward models in Tables 1-5.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds MATH experiments in Table 2 and a clipping ablation in Appendix C, Table 7.

M1.justification: The two-stage correction method remains, but Algorithm 1 corrects the GRPO normalizer from Z to sqrt(max(Z, epsilon)) and replaces the 1/(2N) flip-rate denominators with the corresponding class counts. These are consequential corrections to the specified procedure; the PDFs do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v3 adds mathematical-reasoning evaluation on MATH under synthetic noise, while retaining GSM8K and APPS. This extends coverage within the existing mathematics domain rather than introducing another task family. The clipping experiment uses the existing GSM8K coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain uncorrected GRPO/Dr.GRPO and the mean-only correction comparator where previously evaluated. Table 7's DAPO and PPO labels designate clipping settings within Dr.GRPO, not newly evaluated full baseline algorithms.

E3.justification: New experiments extend model configurations to Qwen3-1.7B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Qwen3-4B, and introduce a 50-step clipping evaluation crossing four clipping settings with three noise levels. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The original experiments retain their reported splits, metrics, 10-epoch budget, and five responses per prompt.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained noise-rate sensitivity and mean-versus-variance correction comparisons, Appendix C adds a controlled test of whether clipping substitutes for denoising. Table 7 examines no clipping, DAPO-style, PPO-style, and tight clipping, identifying a regime where correction's benefit is suppressed or reversed.

E5.justification: Section 6.2 newly quantifies calibration uncertainty using a 95% analytical bound of approximately 0.108 on the estimated signal-retention factor, corresponding to relative bounds of 23.5% and 18.4% for the two reward models. Both versions retain seed=1 disclosures without reporting across-run uncertainty for accuracy.

E6.justification: The accuracy values in v1 Tables 1-5 are retained in v3 Tables 1 and 3-6. New results include MATH performance, such as Qwen3-4B scoring 24.87% without correction versus 31.58% with correction at noise (0.3, 0.4), and the tight-clipping reversal of 34.36% versus 33.13% in Table 7. The main-text code reward-model false-negative rate is also corrected from 0.231 to 0.233, matching the earlier appendix.

T1.justification: v3 adds Theorem 5.4 deriving gradient attenuation and corrected-gradient relationships, and Proposition 5.6 giving a finite-sample noise-estimation bound, with proofs in Appendix A. It also supplies an explicit attenuation-inequality derivation and corrects the surrogate appearing in the estimated-rate improvement bound. The fixed-point comparison itself already appeared in v1, despite its new corollary label.

C1.justification: The core denoising contribution and headline gains of 6.7 points in mathematics and 1.5 in code remain. The contribution list newly claims explicit gradient analysis and noise-estimation sample complexity. The conclusion distinguishes clean population-gradient recovery for Dr.GRPO from variance-adjusted correction for GRPO.

C2.justification: v3 replaces v1's claim of fully recovering noiseless GRPO through the estimated variance with an oracle-versus-consistent-plug-in distinction, and explicitly qualifies the practical improvement guarantee. It adds clipping-related applicability limits and interprets the calibration budget quantitatively. However, its new statement that mean-only correction degrades performance overgeneralizes Table 5: the AceMath row improves from 72.37% to 73.13%.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents the unclipped sequence-level training objective, describes calibration corruptions as numerical modifications or injected code bugs, and supplies the clipping ablation's settings. These expand documentation without establishing changes to the original implementations. Repository access, hardware, runtime, and most hyperparameters remain unchanged; detailed MATH-specific setup information is still absent.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to VerifyBench, One Token to Fool LLM-as-a-Judge, and the MATH dataset, while dropping Ziegler et al. The introduction emphasizes imperfect verifiers, but the positioning against upstream reward-model robustness remains. DISCO's changed author attribution and REINFORCE++'s updated title refer to retained works.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and explanatory transitions throughout the theory are revised. Related-work positioning moves into Background, reward-binarization details move to Appendix B, references move before the appendices, and separate limitations and impact sections appear. Author information and theorem numbering also change.

P2.justification: Document-wide reformatting changes typography, the title and affiliation block, headers, reference columns, and table placement. v3 adds boxed explanatory notes and two tables. Figure 1 retains the same graphic but receives an expanded caption; existing result tables are reformatted and relocated rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves the reliability of the method description by correcting central normalization and flip-rate formulas and qualifying v1's exact GRPO-recovery assertion. The gradient and calibration analyses strengthen the supporting argument, while the clipping ablation tests practical applicability and exposes a failure condition. MATH results broaden validation. Incomplete MATH-specific documentation and the overgeneralized Table 5 interpretation remain weaknesses, but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
